topic.title: Why does anyone live on Tristan da Cunha?

title: Who would settle Tristan da Cunha?
description:
Who would choose to live on Tristan da Cunha, the most remote island anyone lives on?
Tristan da Cunha: no airport, a volcano, and a famous prisoner on the island next door.
Sources: Tristan da Cunha Government, Wikipedia (Sep 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Saint Helena or Pitcairn: which lonely island should we map next? Comment

lines.text: Tristan da Cunha: the most remote island anyone lives on. Who settled here?
Its nearest neighbour, Saint Helena, sits 2,430 km to the north, and South Africa is 2,816 km away to the east.
There's no airport and no runway. To get here, you sail for about a week from Cape Town.
Yet 222 people live here, in one village squeezed between the sea and a volcano, growing potatoes and fishing for lobster.
So why here at all? The clue is on that neighbour to the north.
After losing at Waterloo, Napoleon, the French emperor who had ruled much of Europe, was locked away on Saint Helena, a speck of rock far from Europe.
Britain feared the French would use nearly empty Tristan to rescue him. So in 1816, it sent soldiers and claimed the island.
When the soldiers left, one corporal, William Glass, asked to stay with his family. Sailors and settlers joined them, and their village got a grand name: Edinburgh of the Seven Seas.
Then the volcano erupted right beside the village, and all 264 islanders were shipped to England.
But in England most of them missed home, and they chose to sail all the way back.
So 222 people live on the loneliest island on Earth because one prisoner was once locked up next door.
Saint Helena or Pitcairn: which lonely island should we map next? Tell me below, and look again at Tristan da Cunha.
